method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. claims.claim: **Most drowning causes minimal or no respiratory impairment** and needs no admission beyond a period of observation.
claims.source_text: Most cases of drowning result in minimal or no respiratory impairment and do not require hospital admission beyond a period of observation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **'Near-drowning', 'secondary drowning' and 'wet drowning' are no longer used** and do not influence management.
claims.source_text: Terms such as "near-drowning," "secondary drowning," and "wet drowning" are no longer used and do not influence management
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Timeline:** immersion time; time to and type of basic life support; time to first respiratory effort.
claims.source_text: Immersion time Time to and type of basic life support delivered Time to first respiratory effort
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider supervision and safety:** look for inconsistencies in the story, or a story incompatible with developmental age.
claims.source_text: The cause of drowning should be fully considered including medical causes or issues around supervision and safety … Circumstances leading to the drowning. Consider the following: inconsistencies in story story incompatible with developmental age
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **In a competent swimmer, look for a medical cause:** seizures, hypoglycaemia, arrhythmias including Long QT syndrome, intoxication.
claims.source_text: Consider a medical cause for drowning in children who are competent swimmers, for example: seizures hypoglycaemia arrhythmias and Long QT Syndrome intoxication
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cervical spine injury is uncommon** but consider it with a history of trauma such as diving.
claims.source_text: Cervical spine injury is uncommon but should be considered if there is a history of trauma eg diving
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic, alert children need no investigations**; otherwise be guided by history and condition. **Chest X-ray findings do not correlate with outcome.**
claims.source_text: Children who are asymptomatic and alert require no investigations … Further investigations should be guided by the history and clinical condition … Chest X-ray findings do not correlate with clinical outcomes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Altered mental state without significant hypoxia → look for another cause:** hypothermia, traumatic brain injury, co-existing medical condition, hypoglycaemia.
claims.source_text: Altered mental state in the absence of significant hypoxia should prompt a search for reasons other than drowning as a cause, eg hypothermia, traumatic brain injury, co-existing medical condition, hypoglycaemia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ECG** may help diagnose arrhythmias and Long QT syndrome.
claims.source_text: ECG may be helpful in diagnosing arrhythmias and Long QT syndrome
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Principles: maintain oxygenation, prevent aspiration, stabilise body temperature.**
claims.source_text: Key principles of management are maintaining adequate oxygenation, preventing aspiration and stabilising body temperature
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Vomiting and aspiration of gastric contents are common and a major complication — place spontaneously breathing children in the recovery (lateral decubitus) position.**
claims.source_text: Vomiting is common in drowning victims and aspiration of gastric contents is a major complication. Spontaneously breathing children should initially be placed in the lateral decubitus (recovery) position.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No prophylactic antibiotics.** Reserve antibiotics for signs of infection or sepsis, or the rare submersion in grossly contaminated water.
claims.source_text: Prophylactic antibiotics have no role. Antibiotics have not been shown to improve outcome and should be restricted to patients demonstrating signs of infection or sepsis, or in the rare situation of submersion in grossly contaminated water.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hypothermia is common:** remove wet clothes, dry the child, minimise exposure.
claims.source_text: Hypothermia is a common complication of drowning Remove wet clothes and dry child Exposure should be minimised
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Actively warm to normothermia if core temperature is below 34 °C and there is no evidence of brain injury** — warmed IV fluids, humidified oxygen, forced-air warming blankets.
claims.source_text: Active warming to normothermia should occur if core temperature is less than 34oC and there is no evidence of brain injury. This includes: warmed IV Fluids humidified oxygen delivery forced air warming blankets
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hypoxic brain injury:** there is some evidence for therapeutic hypothermia — **discuss with a paediatric intensivist.**
claims.source_text: There is some evidence for therapeutic hypothermia in children with hypoxic brain injury. This should be discussed with a Paediatric Intensivist
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the paediatric team** for increased respiratory effort, **SpO2 under 95%**, abnormal lung examination, or a suspected underlying medical cause.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Increased respiratory effort SpO2 <95% Abnormal lung examination Underlying medical cause for drowning is suspected
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer** for persisting altered conscious state, respiratory compromise needing assisted ventilation, or ongoing hypoxia.
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Persisting altered conscious state Respiratory compromise requiring assisted ventilation Ongoing hypoxia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Discharge when:** observed **8 hours from the time of drowning**, asymptomatic, normal respiratory examination, **SpO2 ≥95%**, water-safety education given, no ongoing safety concerns, and social work referral made if appropriate.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Observed for 8 hours from the time of drowning Asymptomatic Normal respiratory examination SpO2 ≥95% Education about water safety provided (see handout below) No ongoing safety concerns Referral to social work has been made if deemed appropriate
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Adverse prognostic indicators:** submersion over 5 minutes · effective basic life support after more than 10 minutes · arrival with CPR in progress · GCS under 5 · rectal temperature under 30 °C · arterial pH under 7.1 on arrival.
claims.source_text: Adverse prognostic indicators Submersion time >5 minutes Time to effective basic life support >10 minutes Arrival in hospital with CPR in progress GCS <5 Rectal temperature <30oC Arterial blood pH <7.1 on arrival
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Drowning' (Last Updated June 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Drowning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
